findings.body: The original implementation provided a synchronous `pending_server(&self, state: &str) -> Option<String>` method. Changing it to an `async fn` returning `Result<Option<String>>` alters the function signature and return type. Existing code that calls `flow.pending_server(state)` without `.await` and expects an `Option<String>` will now fail to compile. The same applies to `pending_count`, which was also changed from a sync `fn pending_count(&self) -> usize` to an async `fn pending_count(&self) -> Result<usize>`. These changes constitute a breaking API change and need either to retain the original sync signatures (perhaps delegating to async internally) or update all callers accordingly.
findings.title: Sync methods changed to async break callers

value.summary: Potential API breakage: `OAuthFlow::pending_server` and `pending_count` were changed from synchronous methods to asynchronous ones, which will cause compile errors in existing callers expecting the old signatures.
